body:
As discussed in https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/54196 this is still not really reproduce-able. https://stackblitz.com/github/shulinnn/next-reprod shows (when Stackblitz works) that the click handler works. 

I've also shared a video in the discussion showing how things work fine. We need more data regarding how you experience this issue.

Do you also experience it when you `build` the app?

Did nothing else that create a fresh next.js app and edited the page.js file. Havent tried building it. Could it be brave browser? Cant really try the stackblitz in Brave but in Chrome stackblitz works.
@shulinnn do you, maybe, have JavaScript disabled?
Why would it work for me in 13.4.16 then ?
Alright then, did you try building the app?
Does it work to switch to `console.count`? maybe somehow your `console.log` function is monkey patched?
Still no output with `console.count()` Will try the build later.

Uff this is not looking good. I am worried it is OS specific. 

When you try building, do something like `console.log("FOO1337")`, and then search for that in the `.next` folder. I want to see if its bundled into the client code.

I did not understand, but, did you try with other browsers, same issue?

Yes, i tried Chrome and Brave.Dont have anything else to try it on.
> When you try building, do something like console.log("FOO1337"), and then search for that in the .next folder. I want to see if its bundled into the client code.
It does not get bundled.

Let's try to discard SWC. 

Create a `.babelrc` file, and put this on it:

```json
{
  "presets": ["next/babel"],
  "plugins": []
}
```

That'll opt-out from SWC compiling during dev mode. Does it still not work?
I've been having this exact same problem (in 13.4.18 aswell), eventually I caved in and downgraded to 13.4.16.

> I've been having this exact same problem (in 13.4.18 aswell), eventually I caved in and downgraded to 13.4.16.

Windows too?

Same issue in 13.4.19, Chrome, Windows - `onClick` events were not firing. Downgraded to 13.4.16 and `onClick` events are working.

## Edit
Hot reload wasn't working either in 13.4.19 (I had to refresh to see changes), but it is working in 13.4.16
@ReezanVisram could you try to verify if the handlers are included in the client bundle? And also try to use babel as described above?

The `console.log` is in the `.next` folder in 13.4.16:
![image](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/59345266/e6d8aa0b-f9ff-4f38-bdf8-a2fb7853892b)
But not in 13.4.19:
![image](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/59345266/8640954d-4381-4d79-a609-ce8587156861)

Adding the `.babelrc` didn't add it into the client bundle, and didn't change the behaviour

Uff, this is not looking good. I've tried once again, once with TS on, one with only JS, and it works fine. I am using a Macbook.

It also worked on Stackblitz, which would mean it is not a Linux issue. (https://stackblitz.com/edit/nextjs-twgjnr?file=app%2Fpage.js if it crashes just run `npm install && npx next dev` from the terminal until it works)

I don't have access to my Windows and Linux machines until Monday. And my Windows machine doesn't even have a dev env setup 🤔 

@ReezanVisram, sorry for asking stuff from you once again, but between `13.4.16` and `13.4.17`, there was:

- `13.4.17-canary.0`
- `13.4.17-canary.1`
- `13.4.17-canary.2`

Could you install those, `npm install next@13.4.17-canary.0` for example, and try to figure out which one introduced the breakage?

For anyone with an eagle eye: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/compare/v13.4.16...v13.4.17 maybe you can spot which commit might have introduced a Windows specific issue? I see an SWC update, but I'd expect using `.babelrc` to prevent SWC related issues? Maybe I am wrong there.

@icyJoseph 
- `13.4.17-canary.0` - `onClick` works, there are 3 instances of `FOO1337` in the `/.next` directory
- `13.4.17-canary.1` - `onClick` DOES NOT work, but `FOO1337` is in `server/app` and `/static/chunks/app`  but NOT in `layout.<numbers>.hot-update.js` in the `/.next` directory (maybe these instances just didn't get cleared upon re-compilation because before I downgraded `FOO1337` wasn't present at all in `/.next`, we'd need a fresh project to see though)
- `13.4.17-canary.2` - `onClick` DOES NOT work, but `FOO1337` is in `server/app` and `/static/chunks/app`  but NOT in `layout.<numbers>.hot-update.js` in the `/.next` directory

So I think that it's `13.4.16-canary.1` that introduced the breakage
I also noticed in the Chrome console on `13.4.16`, I get the message `[Fast Refresh]: Reloading` but I don't see that on `13.4.17-canary.1` and `13.4.17-canary.2`. Idk if that helps
